title: Connect your web application to Frontend Observability

blocks.content: Create a Frontend Observability application and get its Faro Web SDK instructions. You need permission to create applications and access to your frontend code; deployment happens after this guide.

blocks.prompt: What origin serves your website? Include http:// or https:// and a port if needed, without a path.

blocks.content: An application groups the telemetry from one frontend. To create yours, complete the following steps:
Open **Frontend Observability**. Every application you create is listed here, grouped into **Active**, **Stale**, and **No data**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Open the application setup wizard.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

steps.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
steps.tooltip: Use a name that distinguishes this frontend from other applications and environments.
steps.description: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.

blocks.content: Set **Allowed origins** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: Use the scheme, hostname, and port your visitors use; add other environments separately.

blocks.content: If your frontend also runs on another origin, use **Add origin**. You can do this later.
blocks.tooltip: List only the origins you intend to monitor; use exact origins for a narrower CORS policy.

blocks.content: Click **Next**. If creation fails, correct the error and try again.
blocks.tooltip: Creating the application does not send browser data; you must still install and deploy Faro.

blocks.content: After the application is created, choose **Manual instrumentation**.
blocks.tooltip: These instructions appear only after the application has been created successfully.

blocks.content: Your application now exists with a collector endpoint waiting for data. Nothing is reporting yet, because your frontend doesn't know about it.
Get your application’s Faro SDK instructions for deployment after this guide:
Choose **NPM** or **Yarn** for this guide and review the installation command for your frontend project.
blocks.tooltip: Use the package manager already used by your project.

blocks.content: Keep **NPM** or **Yarn** selected, then click **Copy** once the application’s Faro initialization snippet loads. Install the SDK and add the snippet to your frontend before deploying.
blocks.tooltip: Wait for your application’s collector URL to load; if configuration loading fails, reopen its SDK instructions and retry.

blocks.content: Click **Continue** to move on to source maps.
blocks.tooltip: You can finish the wizard now and deploy the SDK afterward.

blocks.content: Once you install and deploy the SDK, visits to your website can start sending sessions and errors to this application.
Source maps are optional; continue past them to finish the initial setup.
Click **Continue**. You can set source maps up later from the application settings.
blocks.tooltip: This advances the wizard without requiring a source-map upload.

blocks.content: You can add source maps later to make production stack traces readable.
Leave alerts off for now and return to your applications.
Click **Complete** to return to your applications. Leave the optional alerts off for now.
blocks.tooltip: You can finish setup before telemetry arrives; deploy Faro and visit your website to send events.

blocks.content: Confirm that you are back on the applications page. Your new application may show **No data** until you deploy Faro.
blocks.tooltip: Setup is complete; deployment and a visit to your website are still needed to send data.

blocks.content: The application is configured. Deploy the Faro SDK, then visit your website and use it to generate browser telemetry.

Open your application and check its own recent sessions and errors. It may remain under **No data** until the first events arrive. If it stays empty, check the collector URL, allowed origin, and browser network errors; data from another application does not confirm this one is connected.
